dedupe_keys.name: global roads open access data set version 1 groadsv1

description: The Global Roads Open Access Data Set, version 1 (gROADSv1) combines the best available roads data by country into a global road network, developed under the CODATA Global Roads Data Development Task Group. It uses the UN Spatial Data Infrastructure Transport (UNSDI-T) version 2 data model, country networks are joined topologically at borders and many were edited for internal topology, and the documentation lists the source for each country with road lengths by country. The baseline was compiled by Information Technology Outreach Services (ITOS) at the University of Georgia, and CIESIN at Columbia University updated 27 countries and 6 smaller entities, mostly developing countries with poor data. Coverage is global. The data are free of charge from NASA's Socioeconomic Data and Applications Center through Earthdata Search, as shapefiles and geodatabases by region with maps and documentation; downloads need a free NASA Earthdata login. Users may use and redistribute the data without written permission, except for some countries with extra credits or restrictions named in the documentation. Caveats: road dates range from the 1980s to 2010 by country, most dates are unconfirmed and spatial accuracy varies. It supports global exposure screening and accessibility analysis where national data are poor. It complements GRIP4 and is related to the TIGER/Line roads for the United States.
